o1.biggest_strength: Targets the exact churn pocket with an elegant flat tier that solves both the cost creep and approval workflow objections while keeping existing prices intact.
o1.biggest_mistake: Assumes half of Essentials 8+ customers will willingly pay $15 more per month on day one before they hit 14+ channels, which may be optimistic without strong in-app positioning.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: It is already top-tier, but adding a pre-launch data audit of how many Team accounts actually use multiple users would solidify the cannibalization guardrail.

o2.biggest_strength: The pre-test data check (counting how many Team 8+ accounts only have one active user) is a brilliant, low-effort risk filter.
o2.biggest_mistake: Testing on logged-out new visitors first misses the core problem: proving churn reduction and migration among the existing 3,900 high-churn accounts within the board's two-quarter window.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Shift the validation experiment to existing Essentials 8+ cohorts rather than relying on new-visitor acquisition traffic.

reason: Both arrived at the right strategic move, but Output 1 designed a much better validation test that directly measures churn reduction among existing customers, writes in Buffer's exact voice, and intelligently leverages the yearly billing insight at the point of switch.
